Expect a full evening and a full bill, and take the wine pairing seriously — it is the part the guide singled out.

Akgün wrote it up in Hürriyet in July 2026 and said the quiet part out loud — she hopes it becomes a classic of its kind and lasts, which is not what you write about a room you expect to survive on its own. Come for breakfast or mid-afternoon, when it is not fighting for tables.

Ring +90 533 636 62 30, the number on the venue's own site; Kontuar next door at 67A is +90 533 636 62 73, so read it twice. Prices are not published. No verified coordinate.

name: Nazende Cadde

He goes to the fish and vegetable markets and makes his daily menu and just cooks whatever he wants, but it's out of this world,' Tutak told the BBC. The MICHELIN Guide Türkiye 2026 lists it as a Bib Gourmand — the cheap-and-good medal — with an inspector's note on a menu that changes daily with the market. Note the move: it now sits at Bağdat Caddesi Kınayman B Blok No:345A, not its old Plajyolu Sokak address.
verdict: The two-star chef's favourite table in Turkey costs a fraction of his own — and MICHELIN's inspectors quietly agree.

name: Asmalı Cavit

In his words it sits in a touristy area but mostly local people go: shared dishes cooked with olive oil, seafood appetisers, and the rakı table working the way meyhane culture intends.
verdict: When the city's own cooks want a rakı table after service, this is the address the record keeps agreeing on.
caveat: Evenings only, Sundays never — and it is a rakı-paced meyhane, not a quick dinner.

name: Balıkçı Kahraman
neighborhood: Rumeli Kavağı, Sarıyer · the last quay village before the Black Sea
address: İskele Cad. No:15, Rumeli Kavağı, Sarıyer, İstanbul
recognition: BBC Travel, Nov 2024 — Fatih Tutak: 'It's the Turkish version' of Getaria's Elkano
what_to_order: Kalkan ızgara|Domates salatası|Mısır ekmeği|Meze spread
reservation: Call ahead — it anchors weekend lunches for the whole upper Bosphorus
notes: Kahraman Altun comes from a fishing family, worked 18 years as a cook, and opened his own house in Rumeli Kavağı in 1996; by the house's own history, everyone from waiter to cook is from Trabzon, and the fish is cooked by methods handed down from his grandfather — who rowed from Trabzon during WWI — and his father. Tutak's comparison in the BBC is to Elkano, the Getaria temple of grilled turbot: 'It's the Turkish version.' 'Balıkçı Kahraman is very famous for its turbot. They cook it on a tandoor grill very slowly and season it with salt.'
verdict: A two-star chef puts this village grill in the same sentence as Elkano; the turbot carries the comparison.
caveat: Roughly an hour from the centre — make it the day's destination, and let the season decide the fish.
hot_this_month: The fishing season has been open since 1 Sep 2026 but the lüfer run is reported thin this autumn: ask what came in and what it weighed (checked 12 Oct 2026).

Mesai was a Karaköy fixture, went dark, and came back on İnönü Caddesi in the last days of December 2025 under a glass ceiling, with the strait in front of it and Topkapı, Hagia Sophia and the Maiden's Tower in the frame. It is a night out with a fire counter in it — bar, lighting, a long table — rather than an ocakbaşı you sit at with a rakı and nothing else. Eight months in, it has not been through a full season.

The house says it books through its website only, though a Time Out menu page printed a reservation line, (0532) 056 37 24 - treat the website as the booking route. For him the house is 'the best in the business': 'an artisanal way of making kebabs; hand chopped, with different varieties of meat cuts. They do the best minced kebab and shish kebab.' He compares sitting at the grill while Ahmet Usta cooks in front of you to Japanese robatayaki — one man, one fire, in a neighbourhood otherwise built of plate glass.
verdict: The strongest endorsement a grill can get in this city: the two-star chef eats here on his days off.
caveat: Maslak is a business district, not a stroll — you come for the fire, not the setting. A second, summer branch runs in Türkbükü (Bodrum); make sure you are calling Maslak.

Still fully alive: Oggusto's Cihangir guide of 13 July 2026 lists it serving Van's regional breakfast culture 'geniş sofralarla', and aggregator reviews were coming in within the last month when checked on 17 August 2026.

name: Çakmak Kahvaltı Salonu
address: Çelebi Oğlu Sk. No:6, Beşiktaş çarşı, İstanbul
what_to_order: Serpme kahvaltı|Bal-kaymak|Menemen

notes: The living link to the Beşiktaş kaymakçı: bianet's 2020 report on the kahvaltıcılar streets records that Şah İsmail Çakmak apprenticed under Pando usta in the 1970s before opening his own salon on Çelebioğlu Sokak in 2002 — on the two lanes, Şair Veysi and Çelebioğlu, that now hold some thirty-five breakfast tables. Still firmly in business: Lezzet's Beşiktaş round-up updated 28 November 2025 lists it serving daily 07:00–18:00, and the aggregator listing checked on 17 August 2026 showed it open with reviews from the past two months.
verdict: The honest end of the serpme market — around ₺400–600 a head as of August 2026 — and the only table on the street with a direct line back to Pando.

name: Emirgan Sütiş
address: Sakıp Sabancı Cad. No:1/3, Emirgan, Sarıyer, İstanbul 34467 (per The Infatuation, Sep 2025)
recognition: The Infatuation, Istanbul — Sep 2025, Emirgan Sütiş in 'Alperen Şengün's Favorite Restaurants In Istanbul'
what_to_order: Bal & kaymak|Manda kaymağı|Menemen|Peynirli su böreği|Peynir tabağı
price_range: ₺₺ — à la carte counter; the house publishes no prices online, so budget mid-band and order around the kaymak
reservation: Walk-in; weekend mornings fill the terrace first
notes: The kaymak-and-honey counter as a Bosphorus institution: Sütiş began in 1953 with Mevlüt Kocadağ's first shop in Nişantaşı, and the Emirgan waterfront branch that gave the group its everyday name opened in 1986. Since 2010 the kaymak has started at the company's own 50-hectare farm at Vize in Kırklareli — the house reports 25 tons of milk processed daily against a 50-ton capacity. The Infatuation featured it in September 2025 in Alperen Şengün's Istanbul guide, and the house's own branch list still carried Emirgan when read on 17 August 2026.
verdict: Not a serpme house — you build the spread à la carte around the kaymak. Come at Bosphorus-walk hour, order the buffalo kaymak, and treat everything else as staging.

name: Siirt Şeref Büryan Kebap Salonu
neighborhood: Zeyrek/Fatih · Kadınlar Pazarı quarter, beside the Bozdoğan (Valens) Aqueduct
address: Zeyrek Mah., Ömer Efendi Sok. No:2, 34083 Fatih, İstanbul (Kadınlar Pazarı quarter)
product_tags: Siirt / Kurdish southeast|Pit lamb since 1892 (family claim)
recognition: Culinary Backstreets — 'Siirt Şeref Büryan Kebap Salonu: The Lamb Underground'
what_to_order: Büryan kebabı|Perde pilavı
reservation: None — counter-and-tables kebap salonu; the best of the pit is gone by mid-afternoon
notes: Kadınlar Pazarı, the pedestrian market square beside the Bozdoğan aqueduct, is the closest thing Istanbul has to a Little Kurdistan — stalls of honey, cheese and spice from the southeast ring the pavement. The Avcı family, up from Siirt near the Syrian and Iraqi borders, claim the pit-cooking trade since 1892, and the method has not moved: a side of young lamb goes down a deep hole over coals until the meat turns spoon-tender under a thin crackle of fat, then an usta slices from the cooked sides hanging on hooks and cubes the meat onto flatbread with nothing but salt. The other half of the order is perde pilavı, Siirt's 'curtain' pilaf baked inside a pastry dome. Culinary Backstreets wrote the house up as 'The Lamb Underground', and its maps listing was live and trading at this check.
verdict: The acknowledged büryan house of the Kadınlar Pazarı — Culinary Backstreets' 'Lamb Underground', and the shortest trip to the Kurdish southeast the city offers.
caveat: A plain kebap salonu, not a dinner room — and map listings pin the shop a few steps off the square proper (Ömer Efendi/Serdab corner), so follow the maps link, not memory.

name: Giritli
neighborhood: Ahırkapı/Cankurtaran · below Sultanahmet, near the Marmara walls
address: Cankurtaran Mah., Ahırkapı, Fatih, İstanbul — listings disagree on the exact lane (Keresteci Hakkı Sok. per the house; Akbıyık Değirmeni Sok. No:8 per directories), so trust the maps pin
recognition: In the MICHELIN Guide Türkiye 2026 selection - Bib Gourmand status not confirmed at this check
what_to_order: The fixed meze spread|Wild-herb and olive-oil plates|The day's seafood
reservation: Book — the mansion-garden tables go first in wisteria season
notes: Crete's kitchen crossed the Aegean with the 1923 population exchange, and in Istanbul it landed here, in the garden of a 19th-century mansion at Ahırkapı below Sultanahmet. The format is an island dinner, not a menu: one fixed price buys the full spread of cold and hot mezes in the Girit-Rum register — wild herbs and olive-oil plates from Cretan recipes — then fresh seafood off the grill. The MICHELIN Guide's Istanbul 2026 selection lists Giritli among the city's Bib Gourmands.
verdict: The kitchen the 1923 exchange carried across the Aegean — and the MICHELIN Istanbul 2026 Bib Gourmand list agrees it earns the evening.
caveat: One format, one price, dinner first - not the address for a quick à la carte bite. The terrace is the point and opens in summer; in bad weather service moves to the sister room across the street. Listings disagree on the exact lane, and MICHELIN's listing says it takes no reservations through the guide, so phone first.

name: Hayvore
neighborhood: Beyoğlu · Turnacıbaşı Caddesi No:4, off İstiklal
address: Kuloğlu Mah., Turnacıbaşı Cad. No:4, Beyoğlu, İstanbul
recognition: Culinary Backstreets — 'Hayvore: Lost and Found', the Black Sea specialist of Beyoğlu
what_to_order: Karalahana çorbası|Hamsi tava|Kara lahana sarması|Kuru fasulye with mısır ekmeği
reservation: None — steam-table lokanta; point at the pots
notes: In Laz, the language of the Black Sea highlands, hayvore means 'I am here' — the answer to si sore, 'where are you?', the name of the Black Sea house Hızır Keskin ran before this one. When its regulars were left 'feeling a bit lost, not knowing where to go for a quick, honest lunch of hearty Laz fare', as Culinary Backstreets put it, Keskin answered in 2009 with this steam-table lokanta a few steps off İstiklal — in his own words, 'I decided if I opened a shop again, I would name it Hayvore.' The food is Turkey's culinary misfit: cornbread, collard greens, smoky bean-and-hominy stews that read more Deep South than Aegean, ladled from a line of pots that empty as the day goes. Come in hamsi season and order accordingly.
verdict: The easiest way to eat the Black Sea without leaving Istanbul — a Laz kitchen hiding in plain sight one street off İstiklal, still collecting guide nods in 2026.
caveat: Not a lingering meyhane night — a noisy, fast lokanta, and the day's pots run out; hamsi only in season.
hot_this_month: Hamsi reached Istanbul stalls at about 200 TL/kg around 20 Sep 2026, and the Black Sea shoals are still to come: this is the Laz lokanta for the first hamsi tava (checked 12 Oct 2026).

name: Saruja
neighborhood: Fatih · Akşemsettin Caddesi, the Syrian high street
address: Akşemsettin Mah., Akşemsettin Cad. No:31-A, 34080 Fatih, İstanbul
recognition: Culinary Backstreets — 'Saruja: Return to Mom's Kitchen': 'the very rare eatery that specializes in the traditional home cooking of Damascus'
what_to_order: Sheikh al-mahshi|Waraq enib|Kibbeh labaniyyeh|Shakriyeh
reservation: None — neighborhood dining room, no alcohol; lunch and early evening are its hours
notes: On Akşemsettin Caddesi, where Fatih's shopfronts have quietly turned Damascene, Culinary Backstreets found 'the very rare eatery that specializes in the traditional home cooking of Damascus.' Owner Bilal Khalaf ran computer shops in Syria until the war took them in 2013; as he told CB, he opened here after a month of daily taste tests with his Damascus-born mother at the table, adjusting each dish until it tasted like hers. The register is the one Damascus never used to export: the hot-yogurt home dishes — shakriyeh, sheikh al-mahshi, kibbeh labaniyyeh — that elsewhere exist only at somebody's grandmother's. The Fatih room was open and trading at this check, and a second Saruja now runs in Başakşehir; this one is the original.
verdict: The acknowledged Damascene home-cooking table of Istanbul's Little Syria — dishes that elsewhere only exist at somebody's grandmother's.
caveat: Plain room, no alcohol, no ceremony — this is a family dining hall, and that is precisely its authority.

name: Lale İşkembecisi
address: Tarlabaşı Bulvarı, Taksim/Beyoğlu, İstanbul — the house publishes no street number; use the map link

caveat: Freshest verification is the Culinary Backstreets return visit of 25 November 2025; for a special late crossing, phone first.

name: Midyeci Ahmet
address: Sinanpaşa Mah., Beşiktaş Cd. No:5, 34353 Beşiktaş, İstanbul
tier: SUR LE POUCE — THE HONEST FAST PLATE
what_to_order: Midye dolma|Chilli soslu midye|Midyeci Ahmet tenceresi
price_range: ₺ — counter pricing, per portion
reservation: Walk in.
notes: Ahmet Zeybek's own telling, on the house site: his family carried the mussel trade from Mardin to İzmir in the 1980s, he sold midye outside Istanbul schools from age 7 — 'Hiç okula gitmedim ama hep okul çevrelerindeydim' — opened this Beşiktaş shop in 2014, and after 2019–20 R&D built a 2,000 m2 production plant in Thessaloniki. His mussel-eating contest is what made the name national.
verdict: Midye dolma moved indoors: the street-cart ritual — rice-stuffed mussels, a squeeze of lemon, eat until you stop — with cold-chain sourcing behind it. Purists mourn the cart; parents do not.

price_range: ₺₺ — the house webshop lists 6 cooked rings of uykuluklu kokoreç at ₺2,750 (read 2026-08-17)

The signature is kokoreç wound through with uykuluk — sweetbreads, sold under the house's own 'Ozzie's Makedon Uykuluğu' branding — and the shop now ships it anywhere in Turkey.
verdict: The answer to 'kokoreç worth trusting': a named usta, named sourcing, a shop so sure of its product it publishes prices and couriers the rings nationwide. This is kokoreç as charcuterie, not as a 4 a.m. dare.

name: Kızılkayalar
neighborhood: Taksim — Sıraselviler corner of the square
address: Sıraselviler Caddesi No:2/C, Beyoğlu, İstanbul
tier: SUR LE POUCE — THE HONEST FAST PLATE
what_to_order: Islak hamburger|Et döner|Ayran
price_range: ₺ — büfe pricing at the counter
reservation: None. It is a büfe window on the square.
notes: The house history, on its own site: the büfe's foundations were laid on Taksim Meydanı in 1972 — 'Kızılkayalar Hamburger'in temelleri 1972 yılında Taksim Meydanı'nda atılmıştır' — the Kızılkaya family took it over and, six years on, gave it the family name; it was the first büfe in Taksim to serve et döner, and invented the ıslak hamburger — the small garlicky burger soaked in tomato sauce and held sweating in a steam case — after months of recipe trials. The family brands itself 'Islak Hamburgerin Mucidi', and no one seriously disputes it.
verdict: At 03:00 on Sıraselviler this is not a burger, it is the city's agreed way to end a night: a steam-cabinet case glowing at the corner, one bite gone before you have finished paying. Order two immediately; one is a rookie error.
hot_this_month: Taksim Square holds the state ceremonies on 29 Oct and on 10 Nov before 09:05; expect closures round the corner on both mornings (checked 12 Oct 2026).

name: Develi Samatya
neighborhood: Samatya/Fatih · Gümüşyüzük Sokak, behind the old Marmara sea walls
address: Koca Mustafa Paşa Mah., Gümüşyüzük Sok. No:5/A, Samatya/Fatih, İstanbul
what_to_order: Fıstıklı kebap|Ali Nazik|Özel lahmacun|Develi baklavası
reservation: Phone — big room, terraces fill first on summer evenings
notes: Arif Develi's grandfather took up the kebab trade in Gaziantep in 1912; the family carried the craft to Samatya, the old fishermen's quarter behind the Marmara walls, in 1966. The Samatya house is the original of what is now a twelve-branch, four-generation group — two renovated terraces looking at the Marmara, 400 seats in the open air and around 750 in all. The famous fıstıklı kebap — minced lamb worked through with Antep pistachio — is by the house's own account Arif Bey's personal invention, and the baklava is made on site by masters from Antep, working ingredients shipped up from Antep.
verdict: Where Istanbul goes for Gaziantep when Çiya's field-recording approach isn't the mood — one family, one craft, four generations, Marmara light on the terrace.
caveat: A polished, 750-cover institution, not a hole-in-the-wall — come for the kebab pedigree, not for grit.

The hours are the real advantage: Monday to Sunday, 07:00 to 22:00.

name: Kurukahveci Mehmet Efendi

address: Tahmis Sokağı 66, Eminönü 34116, İstanbul (branch: Söğütlüçeşme Caddesi 12, Kadıköy 34714)

notes: The house is in its 155th year — its own site runs the anniversary as "155. YIL" and its official channel carries the founding date in the handle — and it is still at Tahmis Sokağı 66, in the purpose-built block the company credits to the architect Zühtü Başar. There are only three shops in the whole city, all confirmed on the company's own contact pages: the Eminönü merkez, a Sirkeci branch, and Kadıköy at Osmanağa Mahallesi, Söğütlüçeşme Caddesi 12 — anything sold as Mehmet Efendi anywhere else is retail packaging, not the counter grind. The queue is long, moves fast, and almost everyone in it buys the same thing: Türk kahvesi ground to order and handed over still warm. The company does not publish shop hours on its own site, which is worth knowing before you cross the Golden Horn for it.

name: Karaköy Güllüoğlu
address: Kemankeş Karamustafa Paşa Mah., Kemankeş Cad. No:67, 34425 Karaköy — Beyoğlu
price_range: BAKLAVA
notes: The dynasty's origin is documented outside the family's own marketing: baklava was introduced to Gaziantep in 1871 by Çelebi Güllü, who had learned the recipe from a Syrian chef in Damascus. The city's version was registered as a Turkish geographical indication in 2008 and became Antep Baklavası, a Protected Geographical Indication under the European Commission, in 2013 — the first Turkish product to receive one. This house dates itself to 1843 and puts Nadir Güllü at the counter as "the fifth generation representative of a family that has been making baklava since 1843," trained by his father and master Hacı Mustafa Güllü. The decisive fact is the smallest one: their contact page lists a single shop, Kemankeş Caddesi 67, and OpenStreetMap records the same telephone the house publishes, +90 850 308 45 45, against hours running to one in the morning.

name: Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı
neighborhood: Kadıköy, Asian side — five minutes' walk from the ferry pier
address: Güneşlibahçe Sokağı and Serasker Caddesi, Osmanağa, Kadıköy
notes: The market is not a building, it is a grid of short streets behind Söğütlüçeşme, and Güneşlibahçe Sokağı is its spine — OpenStreetMap maps fishmongers at nos. 1–3, a greengrocer at no. 9, butchers, bakeries and a spice counter inside about eighty metres of each other, with more fish and a butcher's row round the corner on Serasker Caddesi. Buy to the Turkish fishing calendar rather than to a shopping list: commercial fishing runs 1 September to 15 April, so palamut lands from September, lüfer through the autumn and hamsi from late autumn into winter, while between mid-April and the end of August almost everything on ice is farmed levrek and çipura or flown in. Fish is chalked per kilo and cleaned at the counter at no charge; produce is priced per kilo too, and the crates behind the stall are usually cheaper than the display. Stall names on this street turn over faster than the trades do, so shop the counter, not the sign — verify any single shop before you make a special trip for it.
hot_this_month: Palamut is in glut: the 2026 season opened 1 Sep, Istanbul wholesale 59-71 TL/kg in the first week of September; buy it whole and have it cleaned (checked 12 Oct 2026).
